zakat.claim_evidence: The search results for Islamic Foundation of Nevada primarily describe it as a non-profit organization focused on providing education to elementary and secondary school children and offering burial services. There is no explicit mention of 'zakat' on their donation pages or in their general organizational descriptions. While they received a donation from Islamic Relief USA for shooting victims' expenses, this does not indicate that Islamic Foundation of Nevada itself accepts zakat donations from individuals. Other search results mentioning zakat refer to different organizations, such as 'Islamic Foundation' (with a different contact email and phone number) or 'Islamic Society of Nevada'.

With <cite id="13">a perfect score in leadership</cite>, the board shows strong oversight of its <cite id="14">$6.2 million in total assets</cite>. This financial health is further supported by a <cite id="6">working capital ratio of over 31 months</cite>, which far exceeds the standard three-to-six-month benchmark for nonprofits. This allows the foundation to sustain its <cite id="1">educational and burial services</cite> even during periods of revenue fluctuation, such as the <cite id="3">17% decline observed in FY2024</cite>.
rich_narrative.summary: The Islamic Foundation of Nevada (IFN) operates as a religious and educational institution serving the local community through <cite id="1">elementary and secondary schooling</cite> and religious services. In FY2024, the organization reported <cite id="2">total revenue of $2,694,313</cite>, which represented a <cite id="3">17% decline from the previous fiscal year</cite>. Despite this recent decrease in funding, the foundation maintains a <cite id="4">73/100 overall score from Charity Navigator</cite>, reflecting a balanced profile of accountability and program delivery. The organization's financial model is characterized by <cite id="5">high fundraising efficiency</cite>, spending $0.00 to raise every $1 in public support. While the foundation successfully manages <cite id="6">31.4 months of working capital</cite>, its program expense ratio remains a point of neutral observation. In FY2024, IFN reported a <cite id="7">program expense ratio of 75.5%</cite>, which is significantly lower than the <cite id="8">peer program ratio median of 89.8%</cite> for similar education-focused organizations. This gap suggests that a substantial portion of annual revenue is directed toward administrative costs or building reserves rather than direct service delivery. The foundation's impact is most visible through its long-standing initiatives, such as the <cite id="9">Cooley-Moore scholarship program</cite>, which has provided awards for <cite id="10">65 consecutive years</cite>. Additionally, the organization engages in community welfare, including <cite id="11">providing 650 Thanksgiving meals</cite> and reaching <cite id="12">55,000 individuals through health literacy engagement</cite> in recent reporting cycles.
